subject.title: fix(plugin-sdk): update ssrf-runtime import path in cdp-proxy-bypass

question: Should the `fetchConfiguredLocalOriginWithSsrFGuard` and `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` helpers become public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` API, or should the Browser/Ollama package fix preserve owner-scoped private access?
rationale: Both directions can fix the shipped package-subpath regression, but the PR's chosen path changes the public Plugin SDK and SSRF/proxy bypass security boundary, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Access
options.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin owner mechanism or another narrow private seam without adding these helpers to the public SSRF barrel.

options.title: Promote The SDK Surface Deliberately
options.body: Land the public export only as an explicit SDK/security-boundary change with docs, contract updates, guardrail changes, and package smoke proof.

options.title: Pause For Canonical Direction
options.body: Hold this branch until maintainers choose between this public-barrel approach and sibling private-subpath compatibility approaches for the canonical regression.

recommendation.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Access
recommendation.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin owner mechanism or another narrow private seam without adding these helpers to the public SSRF barrel.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is primarily package/public-SDK boundary direction, and the history shows steipete authored the relevant private SDK package-boundary hardening.
